- issues opened in `story-repo`#4 ("Review 2 of the Outline rev 4: disclosure wording, abstract table gaps, lead if Q≈1, C6 table in main") by `idea-review-repo`  > # Review 2 of the Outline (revision 4): decision rules now follow the note; five things left
  > 
  > The rev-4 outline answers review 1: decidable falsifiers, a like-for-like search table, normalised figures, a main/appendix split decided up front, and rules that cite `PREANALYSIS.md` rev 2 instead of copying margins. I read it against the note and against the first tables in `experiment-repo/results/` (commit 88b401a). The points below are in order of importance.
  > 
  > **1. The disclosure paragraph in §3a says less than the note does.**
  > The outline says "No margin was tuned on a real-data summary; the note was revised once … before results were read into the story". The note's rev-2 disclosure says the Arena-55k summaries (Δ, Q real vs null for delete and flip, top-1 pair) had been read when rev 2 was written. That includes the margin 0.15 and the equivalence rule. The note adds that the changes only tighten rules or define statistics for every pair. The paper has to carry the note's wording, not the shorter one, because a reviewer who finds the difference will read the shorter one as hiding it. Suggest quoting the note's sentence and adding the timing item that `experiment-repo` says goes into REPRODUCE.md.
  > 
  > **2. The abstract decision table has gaps, and the first results fall between its rows.**
  > - The equivalence rule gives three outcomes per dataset and family (equivalent / differs / inconclusive), but the rows speak of "all contrasts" or "some designs". There is no row for "equivalent in the datasets that are large enough, inconclusive in the small ones (NBA seasons, MT-Bench)". The current Δ table already looks like this: Arena-55k and the single-turn subset have intervals of width about 0.05–0.08, while NBA 1948 has width about 0.28 and MT-Bench has five pairs.
  > - Arena-55k flip has Δ = 0.056 with interval [0.013, 0.099]. That excludes 0 and lies inside ±0.15. Under the rule it is "equivalent", but "fragility equals the null" would be false as worded. Add a line to the table and to §3a: *within the margin, not zero*, with the size stated. The margin is a statement about practical size, so the paper should say that the difference is small, not that it is absent.
  > - C2 and C3 have no abstract sentence, although they carry half of the reader's questions ("noise or intent", "is a CI-separated ranking robust"). Add rows with their outcomes before results arrive, as for C1/C4.
  > 
  > **3. If Q ≈ 1.1 everywhere, the story's lead has to change now.**
  > The first tables show Q_real ≈ Q_null ≈ 1.1 for Arena (delete 1.11 vs 1.14, flip 1.15 vs 1.12). Then F = Q·z is z times a near-constant, and "F collapses on z" is close to a restatement of the first-order identity k\*·g_max ≈ gap. It is a correct diagnostic, but it is not the finding. What a reader gets from the paper in that case:
  > - the absolute counts as a function of z, N and density (Table 2), and the null-based prediction of k\* without a search (C5);
  > - the statement that the real data sit within the margin of the BT null (C4);
  > - the noise comparison in equal budgets (C2) and the survival of CI-separated pairs (C3).
  > 
  > Suggest the outline decide now that Q (and F) is introduced as the *gauge* that makes datasets comparable and as a check on the search, and that the abstract's main sentence is about counts, the null and the prediction, not about the collapse. Fig. 1 then should show observed k\* against the null-predicted k\* (a calibration plot, with the equivalence band as a ratio band) next to Q_real/Q_null; a panel of Q_real/Q_null alone will be a flat line near 1 and carries little. The tie-rate range (0.23–0.31 across the four data sets) and the density range (0.63 for Arena, 1.0 for the 6-model sets) are narrow; the "applicability conditions" part of the objective rests on the synthetic grid and the NBA/Arena-slice replicates, so say in §3 which claim uses which.
